skill.name: pytest
skill.description: Guides assistants in writing and organizing Python tests with pytest fixtures, parametrization, async tests, mocking, markers, API tests, database tests, and error assertions.
skill.summary: Create and improve Python tests with pytest patterns.
skill.author: bossjones

security_audit.summary: The skill is a benign pytest Markdown guide with no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or unauthorized network behavior. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, local pytest command examples, dummy environment variables, and test variable names. One confirmed issue remains: the parametrization example teaches eval(input), which is unsafe if copied with untrusted input.

remediation.issue: Unsafe eval idiom in pytest parametrization example
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval(input) with a small named function, explicit expected values, or a safe operator mapping so assistants do not copy dynamic evaluation.

remediation.issue: Dummy API key placeholder can trigger secret scanners
remediation.suggestion: Rename API_KEY to TEST_API_KEY and state that test-key is a fake value used only for monkeypatch examples.

content.value_statement: Python teams need reliable tests that stay clear and easy to extend. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through pytest fixtures, parametrization, async tests, mocking, and test organization.
actual_capabilities: Shows basic pytest test function structure and assertions.
Explains fixtures with setup, teardown, scopes, and shared conftest.py usage.
Demonstrates parametrized tests and parametrized fixtures.
Covers async tests and async fixtures with pytest markers.
Provides examples for API, database, marker, mocking, and exception tests.
limitations: Does not install pytest or project dependencies for the user.
Examples assume basic Python and pytest knowledge.
Does not cover every pytest plugin or advanced configuration option.
Some snippets use placeholder functions that must be adapted to the project.

use_cases.title: Add Unit Tests
use_cases.description: Application developers can turn Python functions into clear pytest test cases with direct assertions and parametrized inputs.

use_cases.title: Organize Shared Fixtures
use_cases.description: QA engineers can structure reusable setup, teardown, and fixture scopes across a growing test suite.

use_cases.title: Test Async And API Code
use_cases.description: Backend engineers can plan tests for async operations, API clients, database sessions, and expected failures.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for first pytest coverage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic pytest test plan for this Python function. Identify simple assertions, edge cases, and clear test names before writing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Add Fixtures
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these tests and suggest focused pytest fixtures. Explain which fixture scope each one should use and why.

prompt_templates.title: Parametrize Cases
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these repeated test scenarios into pytest parametrization. Keep case names readable and avoid unsafe dynamic evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Design Integration Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for larger test suites.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a pytest strategy for this service, including unit tests, API tests, async tests, database fixtures, markers, and failure-path coverage.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for tests for a string normalization helper.
output: A concise test plan covering empty input, mixed case, whitespace, and already normalized values.
A set of pytest test cases with clear names, direct assertions, and no external dependencies.

output_examples.input: A QA engineer needs reusable setup for database-backed tests.
output: A fixture design that separates session setup, per-test data, and teardown responsibilities.
Guidance on fixture scope so tests stay isolated and predictable.

output_examples.input: A backend engineer wants coverage for async API behavior.
output: A testing outline for async client setup, success responses, error responses, and expected exceptions.
Marker and organization suggestions for separating unit, integration, and slow tests.

best_practices: Start with small deterministic unit tests before adding integration tests.
Keep fixtures focused and use explicit scopes to avoid hidden shared state.
Use parametrization for repeated cases with the same behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not hide complex setup inside broad fixtures that every test must load.
Do not mix network, database, and unit behavior in one test.
Do not use eval in test examples when direct function calls can prove behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps create, organize, and improve Python tests that use pytest patterns.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The user or agent must run commands in the project environment.

faq.question: Can it help with fixtures?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers fixture setup, teardown, scopes, parametrized fixtures, and shared conftest.py usage.

faq.question: Does it cover async tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes async test and async fixture examples using pytest markers.

faq.question: Is it only for unit tests?
faq.answer: No. It also discusses API tests, database tests, marker selection, and error handling tests.

faq.question: What should users adapt before use?
faq.answer: Users should replace placeholder functions, clients, database models, and paths with project-specific implementations.
